modelAnswer: Democritus believed the shape, size and arrangement of atoms determined the physical properties and sensory feelings (taste, texture) associated with a substance.

stem: Explain the experimental background of atomic theory.

stem: What is correct statement about Al-Ghazali's approach?
Define the theory of necessary causation. How did Al-Ghazali argue against it?
modelAnswer: Necessary causation holds that a cause must always necessarily produce its effect. Al-Ghazali argued instead that what we call cause and effect is only a habitual succession of events willed by God, who can suspend that habit at will, as shown by his burning-cotton thought experiment.

stem: How did Al-Ghazali conclude from a piece of burning cotton? Relate his conclusions to his concept of God's involvement in all natural laws.
keyPoints: ["Al-Ghazali argued that fire does not necessarily cause cotton to burn; rather, God habitually wills the burning each time, and could just as easily will otherwise.","This meant natural \"laws\" are not independent, necessary causes but habitual patterns of God's continuous will, so God can suspend or alter them at any moment (as in miracles)."]

stem: Explain how Al-Ghazali's thought experiment was a challenge to inductive reasoning.
keyPoints: ["Inductive reasoning generalises that because fire has always burned cotton in the past, it necessarily will again.","Al-Ghazali's argument shows this generalisation only reflects a habitual pattern, not a logically necessary causal law, since God could suspend it, undermining the certainty inductive reasoning claims to provide."]

stem: Make an inductive reasoning argument on the reactivity of halogens in the periodic table.
keyPoints: ["Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine are all observed to be reactive non-metals that readily gain one electron to complete an octet.","Inductive reasoning generalises from these repeated specific observations to the broader claim that all halogens are reactive non-metals, since they share the same valence electron configuration (ns2np5)."]

stem: Apply deductive reasoning to the trend in atomic radius along a period in the periodic table.
keyPoints: ["General principle: increasing nuclear charge across a period pulls the same-shell electrons in more tightly, shrinking atomic radius.","Applying this principle deductively to a specific period (e.g. Period 3, Na to Ar) predicts that atomic radius decreases from left to right, without needing to measure each element separately."]

stem: Define inductive and deductive reasoning.
modelAnswer: Inductive reasoning draws a general conclusion from repeated specific observations. Deductive reasoning applies a general principle to a specific case to reach a certain conclusion.

stem: Take some examples from chemistry and apply them to inductive and deductive reasoning separately.
keyPoints: ["Inductive example: observing that several tested metals (Na, K, Ca) react vigorously with water and generalising that alkali/alkaline-earth metals react with water.","Deductive example: applying the general principle that noble gases have a full valence shell to conclude that a specific noble gas, argon, will be chemically unreactive."]
